items.claim: Does Vercel strip a client-supplied `x-vercel-isr` header before it reaches the function?
items.consequence: If clients can send the header through, any visitor can pick which route `_render` or `_isr` renders. That reopens the override #15959 closed and makes this a must-fix security finding. If Vercel strips the header and sets it only on ISR invocations, the change is safe and the ISR 404 fix holds.
items.proposed_fix: A Vercel maintainer, Vercel's documentation, or a test on a real deployment needs to say whether a client-sent `x-vercel-isr: 1` reaches `_render` or `_isr` unchanged, and whether Vercel sets the header on every ISR invocation. If the client header passes through, this candidate reopens as a must-fix finding.

items.claim: `path-override-security.test.js` sends no `x-vercel-isr` header, so it passes at head even though `_render` now honours the query override when that header is present.
